description: ADVANCED LIGHTING RUNG L4 -- SHADOW vs REFLECTANCE EDGES. L2 measured that a shadow EDGE is NOT refused by a LOCAL mechanism (10/12 correct, 0 false, only the two straddling locales refused: a discontinuity is out-of-class for a GLOBAL mechanism and IN-class for a LOCAL one) -- but that identities are recovered on both sides WITHOUT THE SYSTEM EVER KNOWING AN EDGE EXISTS. L4 closes exactly that gap: it ATTRIBUTES the edge. An ILLUMINANT edge scales every channel by ONE factor and so PRESERVES chromatic ratios; a REFLECTANCE edge changes the ratios themselves. THE PREDICATE IS L2'S OWN _slowvar_clause WITH THE QUANTIFIER MOVED FROM SPACE TO WAVELENGTH -- the same cross-multiplied ratio-agreement test with the index pair (locale,locale) replaced by (channel,channel), so no ratio is ever divided into a float. l4_classify_illuminant / _reflectance PARTITION the real edges; l4_flat makes 'not an edge' a POSITIVE datum so a silent classifier cannot score a flawless floor; l4_flood is bo_label's min-flood with Eq(val,val) replaced by the ratio-preserving predicate, so cells joined through illuminant edges share a component and cells across a material boundary do not -- which is how a SHADOW BOUNDARY IS PREVENTED FROM BECOMING AN OBJECT BOUNDARY in the UNMODIFIED vision_border_ownership seed. L4's ASSUMPTIONS ARE STRICTLY WEAKER THAN L2's AND L3's: no reference frame, no compares_to, no SurfaceIdentity codebook, no locale pairing, no spatial registration, no per-locale gain and no pooled scene estimate. It sits BESIDE them, not on top. NO new Rust, NO new constant -- literal set {0.0, 0.5, 1.0}, a STRICT SUBSET of L2's and L3's; the envelope is the four half-step roundings the four observations entering the cross-product carry, and the edge threshold is L1's own falls-out ONE LATTICE STEP. BOUNDED: SINGLE-ILLUMINANT, NEUTRAL-SHADOW attribution. CHROMATIC shadows are NOT handled and PROPORTIONAL materials are IRREDUCIBLY ambiguous -- both are MEASURED as predicted failures, not hidden. MULTI-ILLUMINANT scenes unsolved; L3's 'anchor of the anchor' untouched (L4 uses no anchor); reflectance GIVEN at the cone-triple grain; adjacency GIVEN not grown; the ratio-preserving relation is NOT transitive and l4_flood takes its transitive closure. L4 CLASSIFIES EDGES; IT DOES NOT RECOVER REFLECTANCE -- no L2/L3 arm consumes an L4 attribute. Flag-gated on LightingL4Params.lighting_l4, OFF by default (sec 9 -- default 0 => byte-identical, seed inert), read ABSENCE-TOLERANTLY via MaxOver(default 0), never PickUnique. See VISION_LIGHTING_L4_PREREG.md.

microtheory.label: shadow vs reflectance: an illuminant edge preserves chromatic ratios, so it is a discontinuity that is NOT an object boundary

rules.name: l4_classify_illuminant
rules.comment: THE HEADLINE DECISION. A real edge (the observation changes by more than one lattice step on some channel) across which ONE GAIN EXPLAINS ALL THREE CHANNEL-PAIRS is an ILLUMINANT discontinuity -- a cast shadow, not a material boundary. L2 measured that a LOCAL mechanism recovers identities on both sides of such an edge WITHOUT KNOWING IT IS THERE; this rule is the graph knowing. The envelope is NOT a threshold anyone chose: it is the sum of the four half-step roundings the four observations entering the cross-product carry, plus the second-order term the true->observed substitution costs. Cross-multiplied so no ratio is divided into a float. l4_margin RECORDS the bound's occupancy so its discriminativeness is reported rather than assumed (rung L1b's lesson). Flag-gated, OFF by default (sec 9).

rules.name: l4_classify_reflectance
rules.comment: THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE HEADLINE NON-TRIVIAL. A real edge across which NO single gain explains all three channel-pairs is a MATERIAL boundary. Without this rule the seed could call everything a shadow and score a perfect headline -- which is the refuse-everything disease in its mirror form, and is exactly what the pre-registered Times empty-product positive control injects. It is the EXACT complement of l4_classify_illuminant's predicate, so the two rules PARTITION the real edges. Flag-gated, OFF by default (sec 9).

rules.name: l4_flat
rules.comment: NOT AN EDGE -- as a POSITIVE datum (sec 1.1 clause 4). A change within one lattice step is indistinguishable from rounding. Without this rule an unclassified adjacency would be indistinguishable from a rule that never fired, and a silent classifier scores a FLAWLESS noise floor while measuring nothing. With it, the floor arm can report how many adjacencies got ANY classification and so demonstrate the arm is ALIVE. Flag-gated, OFF by default (sec 9).

rules.name: l4_classify_illuminant_v
rules.comment: l4_classify_illuminant on the VERTICAL adjacency (verdict on the UPPER cell). Present so a 2-D shadow boundary is classified all the way round, not only on its left and right sides.

rules.name: l4_classify_reflectance_v
rules.comment: l4_classify_reflectance on the VERTICAL adjacency (verdict on the UPPER cell).

rules.name: l4_flat_v
rules.comment: l4_flat on the VERTICAL adjacency (verdict on the UPPER cell).

rules.name: l4_flood
rules.comment: THE MERGE, AND THE WHOLE POINT OF THE RUNG: a SHADOW boundary must not become an OBJECT boundary, while a MATERIAL boundary must. l4_val := the minimum l4_val among this cell's RATIO-PRESERVING 4-neighbours (init cid). Fires only when such a neighbour has a STRICTLY SMALLER l4_val, so l4_val decreases monotonically and the flood terminates; at the run_rules fixpoint every ratio-preserving connected component shares its root's cid. THIS IS bo_label's CONSTRUCTION (tools/build_vision_border_ownership.py :176) WITH Eq(val,val) REPLACED BY THE RATIO-PRESERVING PREDICATE -- the same min-flood-to-fixpoint idiom, proven O(N) per sweep under the run_rules drive. Cells joined through ILLUMINANT edges and FLAT adjacencies end up in ONE component; cells across a REFLECTANCE edge do not. Border-ownership, UNMODIFIED, then mints a ProtoObject for the material patch and NONE for the cast shadow -- because the shadow is no longer a component boundary for it to enclose. DECLARED (sec 8): the ratio-preserving relation is NOT transitive, and this flood takes its TRANSITIVE CLOSURE. A chain of individually admissible steps can merge two materials that are not ratio-preserving with each other. NOT tested here; NAMED. Flag-gated, OFF by default (sec 9).
